page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-224 is a high-density general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is powered by dedicated AMD EPYC 7B13 processors offering 112 physical cores and 224 virtual CPUs via simultaneous multithreading. System memory totals 896 GB, preserving a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio at 4 GB per virtual core. Cache architecture features 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache per core cluster. Cryptographic instruction set extensions include AES, VAES, and SHA-NI, alongside AVX, while AVX-512 and AMX extensions are absent. The configuration does not include local storage disks or integrated GPUs, requiring persistent disks or network-attached storage for non-volatile data.

Benchmark results highlight exceptional multi-threaded computational and throughput capabilities. In multi-core CPU benchmarks, the instance achieves top-tier results, reaching a stress-ng score of 302,606.29 and a PassMark CPU score of 115,102.01, supported by top-decile execution in hardware encryption and ray tracing. Memory subsystem measurements confirm top-tier throughput, showing cached read bandwidth of 12,510.38 GB/sec and uncached read bandwidth of 290.62 GB/sec. In application benchmarks, in-memory key-value processing via Redis SET commands reached 187.57 million operations per second. However, single-threaded execution sits within median industry bands, and large-model LLM generation exhibits degraded throughput due to the absence of dedicated matrix accelerators and AVX-512 extensions.

The instance delivers high resource density for workloads requiring massive parallelism within a balanced memory profile. Given the absence of bundled local storage, storage-heavy architectures must factor in network volume throughput. Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-224 fits large-scale compilation pipelines, enterprise web-tier fleets, distributed caching layers, relational database hosting, and multi-threaded analytical computing.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-224 is a general-purpose compute instance equipped with 224 vCPUs and 112 physical cores from AMD EPYC 7B13 processors on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 896 GB of system RAM, adhering to a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation, without bundled local storage or GPU hardware. The server delivers top-tier parallel compute and memory throughput, demonstrated by a stress-ng multi-core score of 302,606.29 and Redis SET throughput exceeding 187 million operations per second. Single-thread execution and unaccelerated large LLM inference remain within moderate tiers due to standard clock profiles and the absence of AVX-512 vector extensions. The instance is structured for distributed caching, large-scale multi-threaded compilation, web serving clusters, and enterprise database operations requiring massive thread counts.
